function.name: calculate_time
function.description: Calculates the time taken to cover a distance at a certain speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

distance.description: The distance to be covered in meters. This is a float type value.

speed.description: The speed at which the object is moving in m/s. This is a float type value.

round_to_nearest_second.description: Optional parameter to round the time to the nearest second.

message.content:
I don’t have direct access to your device’s clock or an up‑to‑date world‑time service from within this chat interface, so I can’t tell you the precise current time.  
If you’re on a computer or phone, simply look at the status bar (top of the screen on most systems) or use a quick command:

* **Windows** – `cmd` → `echo %TIME%`
* **macOS/Linux** – Terminal → `date +"%T"` (shows HH:MM:SS)
* **Smartphone** – tap the home button or lock screen to see the time displayed there.

That will give you the accurate “right now” time for your location.
